content.summary_of_the_paper:
In this paper, the authors propose MotifNet: a neural network-based model that uses position coordinates to represent motif interaction patterns on mRNA. This is achieved by utilizing two separate encoders: one for sequence patterns and one that encodes coordinate information (with implicit neural representation).
The authors apply the model in two different applications: (i) mRNA translation (using data from Sample et al. 2019 that measure mean ribosome load from 5'UTR sequences and (ii) pre-mRNA splicing (using splicing site annotations from Jaganathan et al 2019).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strengths
- Predicting functional sequences of mRNA/pre-mRNA motifs is of extreme importance to biology and drug discovery/development.
- The idea of applying implicit neural representation to model motifs in genomics sequence is new and not yet explored.

### Weaknesses
- The proposed model is very poorly explained and a lot of details and—more importantly—motivation for the design choices are missing. A lot of design choices seems rather ad hoc and the authors did not provide any explanation for them. They also did not show quantitatively why the design choices were chosen.
- The authors did not compare the proposed approach with any previously baseline in any experiment (even though they use Sample 19 and Jaganathan 19 datasets to train their model).
- Please, see below for more “weaknesses”.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is not well written and very difficult to follow. It is full of typos, grammar errors and phrases that do not fit correctly the sentences. The paper also contains many strong claims and no reference (or empirical validation) to validate them. The related work section has many references missing (eg, many works related to neural networks applied to either transcriptional or post-transcriptional regularization). 

The paper also lacks a lot of information for reproduction. It lacks a lot of information about the model (eg the architecture of the two encoders), how to train/evaluate it, which metrics it used, details about the data used to train and evaluate, etc. A small Moreover, source code was not provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: Exploring new ideas for neural network-based modelling of mRNA/pre-mRNA sequences is extremely important for many applications in biology and drug discovery (specially if they are more interpretable). However, I believe this paper is not ready for publication as is. It requires a full rewriting so that the related work section is more relevant, the methods section is more understandable and provide more details so that the experiments can be reproduced. I also believe that some more empirical evaluation is required to justify the utility of the model (both compare with other works and also provide ablations to justify the design choices)
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose a connectionist approach suitable for RNA sequences processing. The main idea is to integrate motif detectors with position encoders so to be able to provide position specific patterns extraction and visualization.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Good:
The aim to obtain efficient motif detectors that are position specific and can be efficiently probed with mutation queries is of interest.

Bad:
The English level is sub-standard and at times hard to follow, several concepts (mostly from the biological domain) are not adequately introduced.

The proposal is a combination of several modules, however a detailed description of each module and how they are jointly integrated (and trained) is missing.
The main idea seems to be: a deep network is used to perform subsampling (this component is not clearly explained, what are the characteristics of this deep model?), then there follows a linear interpolation and then a patter activator layer (still not clearly explained). 
Too many details are missing to understand exactly what is going on. 

Ablation studies are missing: what is the importance of the subsampling and its limits, what are reasonable subsampling rates? what is the sensitivity of the model w.r.t. the size of the PWMs nets?

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a new approach for motif encoding and interaction discovery in mRNA. In particular, it claims to solve the problem of discovering motifs in the first place - if I am correct. For me, the details of the work are hard to understand since the paper uses a lot of jargon without explanation and I have no expertise concerning this biology field. Even after some iterations I don't think everything is clear to me.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
(+) The motif visualizations are beautiful.

(+) The results are analyzed using domain knowledge and meaningful results seem to be obtained.

(-) The paper does not target an ML audience since it uses a lot of jargon without explanation, for example the below. The audience obviously needs no detailed introduction but an idea of what the text is about would be helpful.

- TF factor motifs
- amino acid coding codon
- tandem repeats
- in-frame upstream AUG, out-of-frame AUG
- crosslinking immunoprecipitation sequencing
- TACTAAC branch point pattern and GC-rich sequence pattern.

(-) The paper seems to claim to solve the problem of discovering motifs ("The common limitation of these methods is that if we don’t have the domain knowledge of a certain motif pattern, there is no way to search a sequence pattern along the sequence samples at the first stage."), however in Eq. 2 the input vector a seems to contain patterns. It is left unclear where they come from and what they encode exactly.
"If a region of certain position U in sequence is known as important, we can establish motif generation process as denoted in Algorithm (1)"
- how do we know if a region of certain position U in sequence is known as important?

(-) The model definitions are a bit unclear:
- What is C, does "PWM-like pattern activation layer" refer to the above-mentioned 1D convolution?
- Where does the p_i come from in (1)

================================================================================

Some Minor Comments

- beween a notion and the abbreviation, leave a space
- p.3 "For each nucleotide base S iit will multiple the weight score" - multiply?
- p.4 "integrate deep network feature into a shallow layers" -> layer
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is not written clearly. The evaluation seems to be of high quality from a biology standpoint and to contain novel results. Code is not provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: Altogether, I think do not think the paper is understandable by the ML community and thus I wonder what potential it could have on future ML research. I might be missing something completely but I really took time to read the paper in detail. The evaluation is detailed and it might represent a great contribution if the model's presentation gets improved considerably.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.strength_and_weaknesses: The idea seems interesting. However, the evaluation of the model is quite lacking. There is no comparison with existing methods, which makes this exposition incomplete.
content.summary_of_the_review: The model proposed in the paper is interesting but there is no comparision with existing methods. Further some of the claims about motifs discovered are hard to evaluate in this venue (such as the claim that "violation of some motif patterns from motifNet in real human mRNA variants will significantly cause disease related cell dysfunction"). A biology conference/journal may be a better place for this.
